guidance: Planning estimate from the endurance rating a vendor publishes, not a warranty decision or a failure prediction. The rating covers host writes at the workload it was measured at, so a different write mix, temperature or retention can change how long a real drive lasts; compare the drive's own S.M.A.R.T. data units written with the rating before retiring it.
method: Endurance is published either as TBW, the host data a drive is rated to absorb over its rated period, or as DWPD, the number of times the whole drive can be written each day for that period, and the two are one figure: TBW = DWPD x capacity x 365 x years, with capacity in decimal terabytes. An 800 GB drive at 10 DWPD for five years carries 14,600 TBW, and a 960 GB drive at 0.8 DWPD for five years carries 1,401.6 TBW. The page accepts either form, reports the other, and gives the daily write budget TBW x 1,000 / (365 x years) in GB per day. Your load is entered as host writes per day in decimal GB: the drive writes per day it represents is that figure divided by the capacity in GB, the writes per year are daily writes x 365 / 1,000 in TB, the share of the rating used each year is the writes per year divided by TBW, and the projected life is TBW divided by the writes per year. A projection that lands exactly on the rated period counts as covered; one GB per day above the rating does not. TBW is a host-write figure measured against the vendor's rated workload and already contains that workload's write amplification and over-provisioning, so it is not a raw NAND-endurance number, and a different mix of random and sequential writes can consume it at a different rate. The projection assumes the entered daily rate for the whole life and does not model temperature, retention or firmware changes; a drive in service can be compared with its own S.M.A.R.T. data units written. Capacity is accepted from 1 GB to 100,000 GB, the rated period as a whole number from 1 to 10 years, TBW from 1 to 1,000,000 TB, DWPD from 0.01 to 1,000, and daily writes from 0.1 to 1,000,000 GB, with a field-specific refusal outside each range. Twelve published Western Digital SN640 rows and the Samsung 845DC PRO 800 GB / 10 DWPD / 14,600 TBW rating were replayed against the page to their printed precision.
